Explanation:

-Improved wheat varieties (TD1, Faisalabad 08, AS2011, Galaxy 2014) have good yield than earlier varieties. The new varieties seed color is red and old one’s brown. It is better in chapati (bread) making. Come frequently from XX province
-Rice hybrid seeds of coarse variety IRRI 6 (Guard50, Guard402), better than the old ones. Need shorter time and gives more yield, saves some labour
-Reaper, used to harvest wheat, the straw is not wasted, available on rent (2 kg grain/40 kg)
-Zero tillage has been used for 3 to 4 years
-Combine harvester, also available on rent
-Micro nutrients such as (zinc) used in rice is helpful and increases yields in rice crop
-Water courses are lined and created and now water reaches earlier and help timely planting of crops
For men
-Wheat reaper saves time and labour
-Zero tillage grown crops need less water, no land leveling is needed, no additional ploughs are needed, gives good yield
-Improved varieties saves time and yield more
For women
-Reaper: the women had to harvest, now in many areas they don’t have to harvest due to reaper.
-The benefits of zero tillage technology, improved seeds, combine harvester are also shared by women and other family members.

Yes, the farming areas in which they are involved such as crop sowing, planting, harvesting, weeding, threshing, collection they can get the benefits of new farming practices along with other family members. But young men have more roles in variety selection etc. than young women. They can have a role in selection of a variety good for bread making.

Bhotar (ladnd lord) brings in the new innovations and practices. He is more benefited. We also advise him.

Women are given certain agricultural activities keeping in view their household responsibilities and their capacity. These work allocation has been followed for decades and only with the introduction of new technology, the customs are likely to change.
When they get educated and find alternative livelihood then they don’t follow. Only in poor families the women do the farming works, in prosperous families it is considered as an indignity.

-The household head (father) decides who is to be given which plot. Women’s are usually given the easier tasks, and the nearby plot. The tasks a women is supposed to do on the plots are already known.
-They have only shared plots. Man may also help her wife at farm.

-When a lot has to be done in a shorter time. For example, weeding in onion, needs large labour and has to be done in a shorter time, the household member join men or women. Similarly, at harvest of crop and vegetable picking time other household members work together and help each other. The household members also help women in raring livestock.
-Generally it is not women job to decide to plant a new crop. However, she can help her husband in this decision and her husband may also consult her.
-They think themselves and then consult with the elders (father, elder brother or other family member)

-While a man decide himself when it is a 4-8 acres crop. The larger farms are managed by tenants, the land lord then consult with their tenants, or with elders/experience one or someone from agriculture department about planting a new crop. The tenant (Raak) on his own land decides himself about the crop. Very few Bhotars work on their lands themselves.
